title: Generic constancy of the number of geometric irreducible components
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For each $t\in Y$, write $X_t$ for its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], over the residue field $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and choose a separable closure $\kappa(t)^s$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Count the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)^s$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every $y\in Y$ there are a nonempty relatively open subset $V\subseteq\overline{\{y\}}$ and an integer $n\geq0$ such that this number is exactly $n$ for every $t\in V$. The assertion holds for any choices of the separable closures; no flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on $f$ or $Y$ is required.

source.place: Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good), with the geometric-component-count convention of Tag 0556 (lemma-base-change-fibres-nr-geometrically-irreducible-components). Finite type makes each geometric fibre Noetherian, so the constant value is a finite nonnegative integer.

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$ and let $S$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{\{y\}}$. Its underlying space is this closure and has generic point $y$: the closure of a point is irreducible, since if it is covered by two closed subsets, the one containing the point contains its closure. Form $h:X_S=X\times_Y S\to S$. This is finite type by base-change stability. The base-change count theorem gives $n_{X_S/S}=n_{X/Y}|_S$ and independence from all separably closed extensions. It therefore suffices to find a nonempty open of $S$ on which this function has one finite value. In the remaining steps rename $X_S,S,h,y$ as $X,S,h,\eta$; thus $S$ is irreducible and $\eta$ is its generic point.

The generic fibre $X_\eta$ is finite type over $k=\kappa(\eta)$. Apply generic component splitting to choose a field $L$ and a finite etale morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ such that every irreducible component of $G=X_\eta\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$ remains irreducible and nonempty after every extension of $L$. Base-change stability makes $G$ finite type over $L$. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole field), so the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem and the finite-components theorem give a finite list of distinct components $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ covering $G$. Allow $n=0$, in which case $G$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 055A, proof paragraph 2; Tag 0551, generic field splitting

proof.text: Apply the geometric generic-cover spreading theorem to $h:X\to S$ with the specified $L,a$ and the closed cover $(A_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$. Its geometric-irreducibility hypothesis is precisely the component-splitting conclusion of Step 2. Obtain an open $W\subseteq S$ containing $\eta$ such that, for every $s\in W$ and every field extension $K/\kappa(s)$, there are a continuous surjective scheme morphism $p:Z\to (X_s)_K$ and a cover of $Z$ by $n$ nonempty irreducible subsets $B_i$. Each $\overline{p(B_i)}$ is irreducible and closed, and these $n$ subsets cover $(X_s)_K$. Every irreducible component $D$ of this fibre lies in one of them: apply irreducibility to the finite closed cover $D=\bigcup_i(D\cap\overline{p(B_i)})$. Maximality then gives $D=\overline{p(B_i)}$. Thus the fibre has at most $n$ components. For $n=0$, the cover forces $Z$ empty and surjectivity forces the fibre empty. In particular $n_{X/S}(s)\leq n$ on $W$.

source.place: Tag 055A, proof final paragraph, upper bound; geometric-cover spreading is the existing Tag 055G closure-and-shrinking input

proof.text: Spread the specified finite etale field map $a$ using the etale generic residue-field model theorem. It gives an etale morphism $g:T\to S$, a generic point $\xi$ of $T$ with $g(\xi)=\eta$, and an isomorphism $r:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}L$ compatible with the maps to $S$. Set $P=X\times_S T$ and $q:P\to T$, which is finite type by base-change stability. Associating the fibre products and using $r$ identifies $P_\xi$ with $G$: both are the pullback of $X\to S$ along the same field-valued point of $S$. Therefore $T$ is irreducible with generic point $\xi$, and its generic fibre has exactly $n$ ordinary irreducible components.

source.place: Tag 055A, proof paragraph 2; the field-splitting and etale model portions of Tag 0551

proof.text: Apply the ordinary component lower-bound theorem to $q:P\to T$ and $\xi$. The hypotheses hold by Step 4, including finite type and the finite generic component count $n$. Obtain a nonempty open $U\subseteq T$ on which every ordinary fibre $P_t$ has at least $n$ irreducible components. Because $\xi$ is generic, $\xi\in U$.

source.place: Tag 055A, proof final paragraph, invocation of Tag 0554

proof.text: For $t\in U$ and a separable closure $K$ of $\kappa(t)$, the projection $(P_t)_K\to P_t$ is surjective: $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is surjective and surjectivity is stable under arbitrary base change. Both schemes have finitely many irreducible components, since they are finite type over fields, hence Noetherian. Write the geometric fibre as a union of $m$ irreducible components. The closures of their images are $m$ closed irreducible subsets covering $P_t$. The finite closed-cover and maximality argument of Step 3 shows that each ordinary component is one of these closures; hence the ordinary count is at most $m=n_{P/T}(t)$. Step 5 gives $n_{P/T}(t)\geq n$. This also covers the empty case $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 055A, proof final paragraph, ordinary lower bound implies geometric lower bound

proof.text: Let $U_0=U\cap g^{-1}(W)$. It contains $\xi$, because $g(\xi)=\eta\in W$, so it is nonempty and open. Etale openness shows that $V=g(U_0)$ is a nonempty open subset of $S$ contained in $W$. For every $s\in V$ choose $t\in U_0$ with $g(t)=s$. By base-change invariance, $n_{X/S}(s)=n_{P/T}(t)\geq n$; by Step 3, $n_{X/S}(s)\leq n$. Thus it equals the finite integer $n$. Step 1 identifies $V$ with a relatively open nonempty subset of the original $\overline{\{y\}}$ and identifies the component-count functions there. Independence from all choices of separable closure was included in Step 1, and no flatness or Noetherian hypothesis was added.

source.place: Tag 055A, proof paragraph 2, open descent, combined with final paragraph and Tag 0556
